newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Senate clears private funds bill.
newsitem.headline: Romania Senate clears private funds bill.

text.p: Romania's upper chamber of parliament passed a long-awaited bill to turn five regional private ownership funds (FPPs) into U.S.-style mutual funds as part of a mass selloff.
"The Senate approved the bill on the FPPs' turning into investment companies with 91 votes for, one against and seven abstentions," Senate spokesman Mihai Corut said on Tuesday.
The bill has yet to clear the lower Chamber of Deputies before it becomes a law.

The FPPs were created under a 1991 privatisation law as administrators of a 30 percent stake in around 6,500 state companies on behalf of 15.5 million adult Romanians who got free pre-share vouchers representing that stake in 1992.
The majority 70 percent stockholder of the 6,500 enterprises is the centrally-run State Ownership Fund.

Conversion of the FPPs into investment companies is part of a mass privatisation started last year which offered adult Romanians stakes of up to 60 percent in around 4,000 state companies in exchange for vouchers and coupons.
Romanians could also opt for placing their privatisation paper with one of the five regional FPPs in return for shares of these funds ahead of their conversion into investment firms.
Under the Senate-approved bill the FPPs, scheduled to turn into investment companies starting November 1, will give Romanians shares equivalent to the dividends the FPPs amassed since their creation.

This is an amendment to the original government version which said those dividends should form a fund to serve projects of social interest if any money was left after Romanians redeemed their share in cash.
Shares of the FPPs turned into investment companies can be traded on Romania's capital market, according to the bill.
A stock exchange has been operating in Romania for almost a year and the country is now getting ready for an over-the- counter market scheduled to go into trading later this month.

Brokers welcomed the bill on the transformation of the FPPs saying the new investment companies could become the big investors the stock market needs to pick up in liquidity. -- Lull Popes, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
